//read-tree: read-tree ASKS rather than allows, deliberately; the asymmetry with hash-object is not an oversight to tidy away. hash-object only ever writes a LOOSE OBJECT (additive, unreferenced, gc-collected) and cannot overwrite anything. read-tree writes the INDEX, and with -u / -m -u / --reset it updates the WORKING TREE, silently overwriting uncommitted files — the same capability that puts checkout, switch, restore and clean in the ask list. The schema is verb-level (deny|ask|allow), so allowing the verb would allow every flag with it.
reason: Raw git is denied for this subcommand. These run without asking: status, add, log, diff, show, blame, shortlog, describe, rev-parse, rev-list, ls-files, ls-remote, cat-file, merge-base, diff-tree, diff-index, diff-files, hash-object, version, help, check-ignore. These prompt instead of failing: clone, worktree, stash, branch, tag, fetch, pull, remote, checkout, switch, restore, apply, push, commit, reset, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, clean, read-tree. Anything in neither list is denied here, so pick the nearest listed verb or ask the owner. Note: plugin git via ctx.subprocess (dsh-worktree, dsh-git-plugin) bypasses this guard — it gates only model bash calls.
